title: FuzeInfra credential hand-off registry
description: Maps a credential FuzeInfra owns (a Secret in the fuzeinfra namespace) to the consumer namespace + Secret name it must be re-sealed for. This file IS the authorization decision: publish-sealed-handoff.yml will only ever seal a source listed here, for the target listed here. See docs/CREDENTIAL_HANDOFF.md.

id.description: Stable identifier. Used as the workflow input and in branch names.

enabled.description: Gate. A disabled entry is never sealed and never verified.

consumerRepo.description: owner/repo that receives the sealed ciphertext and owns the alert.

source.description: Where FuzeInfra holds the authoritative plaintext, in-cluster.

target.description: The consumer scope the value is sealed FOR. kubeseal --scope strict binds the ciphertext to exactly this namespace + Secret name, so it is inert anywhere else.

format.description: How the source value is rendered into the target key. 'raw' seals the password verbatim. 'postgres-url' composes postgresql://<verify.username>:<password>@<verify.host>:<verify.port>/<verify.database> — which is what consumers actually consume (MendysRobotics' mendys-secrets/DATABASE_URL), and it REQUIRES the verify block.

manifestPath.description: Repo-relative path in the CONSUMER repo where the SealedSecret manifest lives. No leading slash, no '..'.

branch.description: Consumer base branch the hand-off PR targets.

verify.description: How the periodic detector proves the credential the consumer ACTUALLY holds still authenticates. Omit to skip verification (and say why in notes).

host.description: In-cluster DNS name, <service>.<namespace>[.svc.cluster.local]. Both halves are load-bearing: it is embedded verbatim in a 'postgres-url' value AND split into the service/namespace the verifier port-forwards to.
